sources.quote: During this time period there were 70 instances when the City's chloride dioxide levels were higher than the standard set by the EPA, and ranged between 0.85 to 2.04 milligrams of chlorine dioxide per liter.
sources.searcher_note: Reprints the city's self-report: samples July 24, 2020 through March 6, 2022 over the EPA limit, generator fault. Counts 70 exceedance instances, not monthly violations.

sources.quote: The City recently learned water samples taken July 24, 2020 through March 6, 2022 at its Aqua Viva Water Treatment System revealed levels of chlorine dioxide exceeding the maximum levels for drinking water established by the EPA.
sources.searcher_note: Original city release 'City Self-Reports Compliance Issues to ADEQ' (March 2022). Page returned 403 to the fetcher; quote taken from Signals AZ's verbatim reprint and search snippets of this page, so it may only verify via the archive copy.

sources.quote: Yuma's drinking water was tested to have multiple instances of higher than regular chloride dioxide levels.
sources.searcher_note: Earliest press found; local TV report of the city's self-report, cites a generator problem, no dates or levels

notes: The 2020-2022 exceedances were public in March 2022 through the city's own self-report to ADEQ and local press (KYMA, Signals AZ). The city counts 70 instances at 0.85-2.04 mg/L; the lead counts 21 monthly acute violations at 0.9-2.0 mg/L over the same Jul 2020-Mar 2022 window. The city says it 'recently learned' of them in March 2022, and search snippets say it notified customers once aware. No source found on the national comparison (21 of 54 acute chlorine-dioxide violations since 2015), on the May 2022 arrival in federal records, or on any ADEQ enforcement action. City fact sheet and EWG page returned 403. A separate, later exceedance (June 7, 2025, 1.15 mg/L, per KYMA 2025-06-10 and city update snippets) is outside the lead's window.
